lab_tests: Lactose hydrogen breath test (gold standard, non-invasive)
Lactose tolerance test (blood glucose after lactose load)

thresholds.hydrogen_breath_test: >20 ppm rise in breath H2 above baseline after 25-50g lactose load → positive
thresholds.genetic_LCT: -13910 C/C genotype → lactase non-persistence (common in East Asians)

clinical_features: Watery diarrhea (30 min to 2 hours after milk/dairy)

treatment.indication: When dairy consumption cannot be avoided
If dairy intake is severely restricted

prevention: Secondary prevention: adequate calcium from non-dairy sources (leafy greens, tofu, fortified foods)

clinical_examples.description: A 28-year-old woman from Guangzhou reports bloating, cramps, and watery diarrhea 30-60 minutes after drinking milk or eating ice cream. Symptoms began in her early 20s. She avoids dairy now and symptoms resolve. Lactose hydrogen breath test: baseline H2 5 ppm → 75 ppm at 90 min (positive).
clinical_examples.key_findings: Temporal relationship with dairy + positive breath test → adult-type lactose intolerance
clinical_examples.outcome: Diagnosed with adult-type hypolactasia (lactase non-persistence). Advised on lactose-free alternatives and calcium-rich non-dairy foods (Chinese broccoli/gai lan, tofu, fortified soy milk). Lactase enzyme supplement for occasional dairy consumption.
